headline: Dubai has started a four-week trial of driverless electric pods that run on their own narrow tracks away from regular traffic.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a real public trial of a driverless transit system, but a four-week test at one site.
importance_line: If the trial goes well, commuters in Dubai could one day get on-demand rides without drivers or timetables, but this is a four-week test at one site and the cost savings are the authority's own claim.
summary: Khaleej Times reports that Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) began a four-week trial on 11 October at Bluewaters of the Glydways system, whose driverless electric pods carry four to six passengers at up to 50 km/h on dedicated guideways, with RTA chief Mattar Al Tayer taking a five-minute ride. RTA says the test will check safety, reliability and passenger experience, and it claims the system could cost up to 90 per cent less to build and 70 per cent less to run than comparable transport, figures that are the authority's own and still untested.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text. Status CONFIRMED for the launch (official RTA event); performance and cost figures are RTA claims.
